clubs.description: America's largest motorsport club — autocross, road racing, rallycross, and time trials, with events in nearly every state and a famously low barrier to entry.
clubs.name: Sports Car Club of America (SCCA)

clubs.description: Founded 1952. Tours, concours, driver schools, and the largest single-marque community in the US. If you own a BMW, this is home base.
clubs.name: BMW Car Club of America

clubs.description: The largest Porsche club in the world. Driver education days, club racing, and the annual Parade — the single-marque calendar's center of gravity.
clubs.name: Porsche Club of America

clubs.description: The US home for Ferrari owners — concours, rallies, and track weekends organized around the cars Maranello built.
clubs.name: Ferrari Club of America

clubs.description: The Mustang's official fan body since 1976 — shows, judged concours, and regional clubs in most states.
clubs.name: Mustang Club of America

clubs.description: The country's oldest and largest antique-car organization (founded 1935). If it has wheels and history, there is a class for it at an AACA meet.
clubs.name: Antique Automobile Club of America

clubs.description: Runs the Goodwood Revival and Members' Meeting — period-correct historic racing at its most serious and most stylish. The waitlist is part of the ritual.
clubs.name: Goodwood Road Racing Club

clubs.description: The German home of Porsche enthusiasm — officially recognized clubs for everything from the 356 registry to modern GT cars.
clubs.name: Porsche Club Deutschland

clubs.description: Japan's official body for classic and historic vehicles — the organizing force behind the country's concours and classic rally scene.
clubs.name: Automobile Club of Japan (Classic division)

clubs.description: Not one club but a worldwide Saturday-morning institution: informal dawn meets in parking lots from Irvine to London. Find your local chapter, show up early, leave before the burnouts.
clubs.name: Cars & Coffee

clubs.description: The umbrella for British car clubs in North America — MG, Triumph, Austin-Healey and more, with a full calendar of shows and tours.
clubs.name: North American Council of British Car Clubs

clubs.description: Dedicated to the rotary engine's survival — RX-7 and RX-8 owners, rebuild knowledge, and track days where the brap is mandatory.
clubs.name: Rotary Car Club

clubs.description: The Miata community's backbone — gap runs, tech days, and the annual Miatas at the Gap gathering in the Smokies.
clubs.name: Miata Owners Club network

clubs.description: Toyota and Lexus 4x4 owners — trail runs, recovery training, and the deepest Land Cruiser technical knowledge base in North America.
clubs.name: TLCA (Toyota Land Cruiser Association)

clubs.description: The grassroots core of American hot rodding — local clubs, cruise nights, and the Goodguys national show series as the tentpole calendar.
clubs.name: Goodguys-affiliated local clubs

clubs.description: Keeps air-cooled Volkswagens on the road — swap meets, campouts, and a parts network that has saved thousands of Beetles and Buses.
clubs.name: Vintage Volkswagen Club of America

clubs.description: The Corvette's national body — museum delivery culture, caravan tours to Bowling Green, and judged shows for every generation from C1 to C8.
clubs.name: National Council of Corvette Clubs

clubs.description: The Mercedes-Benz club for the US — technical sessions, concours, and a star-studded annual calendar for everything from Pontons to AMGs.
clubs.name: Mercedes-Benz Club of America

clubs.description: The entry point to organized off-roading — local clubs teach trail etiquette, recovery, and land stewardship. Most Jeep owners find their people here first.
clubs.name: United Four Wheel Drive Associations network

clubs.description: London's modern classic and supercar meet scene — dawn runs, show fields, and the strongest Sunday-morning calendar in Europe.
clubs.name: Sunday Scramble (Bicester Heritage)

clubs.description: Australia's historic motoring federation — club plates, rallies, and preservation for a car culture with deep local manufacturing roots.
clubs.name: Australian Historic Motoring Federation clubs

clubs.description: Canadian classic and collector clubs under one umbrella — shows, tours, and advocacy for collector plates and insurance.
clubs.name: National Association of Automobile Clubs of Canada network

clubs.description: The American home of Alfisti since 1951 — tours, track days, and the annual national convention, with local chapters in most states and deep knowledge of everything from Giuliettas to the Giulia Quadrifoglio.
clubs.name: Alfa Romeo Owners Club (AROC-USA)

clubs.description: Founded in 1958 to preserve Cadillacs and LaSalles of every era — fin cars to Blackwings. Its authenticity manuals and judging standards are the reference for the marque.
clubs.name: Cadillac & LaSalle Club

clubs.description: North America's Lotus club since 1973, running the annual LOG (Lotus Owners Gathering) — the largest Lotus meet in the country — plus tours and track days for everything from Elans to the Emira.
clubs.name: Lotus Ltd.

clubs.description: Chapter-level competition in the Bay Area: autocross, road racing at Laguna Seca and Sonoma, and rallycross. The working example of the SCCA's chapter model — show up with a helmet and a road car.
clubs.name: SCCA — San Francisco Region

clubs.description: One of the PCA's most active regions: Bay Area tours, autocross, and driver-ed weekends at Laguna Seca and Thunderhill. Chapter life at full strength — the level of local data the atlas is now collecting.
clubs.name: Porsche Club of America — Golden Gate Region

clubs.description: The UK's Trident community since 1972 — concours, tours, and a technical archive for the classic cars, with the modern Nettuno generation folded in as the club's second era.
clubs.name: Maserati Club UK

clubs.chapterModel: Regional meets and an annual reunion in Auburn, Indiana
clubs.description: The club for the three Cord-era marques — Auburn, Cord and Duesenberg — founded in the 1950s and anchored by the annual Labor Day reunion in Auburn, the hometown of the Auburn Automobile Company.
clubs.name: Auburn Cord Duesenberg Club

clubs.description: Packard's national club since 1952 — regions, tours, a judged national meet, and the deepest restoration knowledge base for everything from Twin Sixes to the last South Bend cars.
clubs.name: Packard Automobile Classics (The Packard Club)

clubs.chapterModel: Single national club with an annual convention
clubs.description: The North American home of Saab owners since 1981 — the annual Saab Owners' Convention, a parts-and-knowledge network that outlived the factory, and a quarterly magazine for two-stroke to Turbo X alike.
clubs.name: Saab Club of North America

clubs.description: Studebaker's driver-focused club since 1962 — chapters in most states, an annual international meet, and a monthly magazine; the practical knowledge pool for keeping Hawks, Larks and Avantis on the road.
clubs.name: Studebaker Drivers Club

clubs.chapterModel: Single national association with regional events
clubs.description: The DMC-12's owners' association, serving the one-model marque since the 1980s — technical support, events, and the social centre of a community built around a single, unmistakable car.
clubs.name: DeLorean Owners Association

clubs.description: Pontiac and Oakland's international club since 1972 — the GTO and Trans Am knowledge base, judged shows, and the annual convention that keeps the excitement division's flag flying after the marque's closure.
clubs.name: Pontiac-Oakland Club International

clubs.description: Oldsmobile's national club — chapters, judged nationals, and preservation for the full 107-year run from the Curved Dash to the Aurora, with the Rocket-era cars at its heart.
clubs.name: Oldsmobile Club of America

clubs.description: The home of Hudson, Essex and Terraplane owners — a national meet, regional chapters, and the parts and step-down knowledge base for everything from Essex Super Sixes to Twin H Hornets.
clubs.name: Hudson-Essex-Terraplane Club

clubs.description: Nash's national club — the Nash Times magazine, an annual meet, and the registry knowledge for Ambassadors, Ramblers, Metropolitans and Nash-Healeys alike.
clubs.name: Nash Car Club of America

clubs.chapterModel: Regional chapters and an annual national meet
clubs.description: Founded in 1959 for the cars of Kaiser, Frazer and the Kaiser-era Willys lines — a monthly bulletin, a manufacturing fund reproducing unobtainable parts, and the Henry J and Darrin registries.
clubs.name: Kaiser Frazer Owners Club International

clubs.chapterModel: Single national club with the annual Grand Stutz meet
clubs.description: The registry and knowledge base for Stutz and Black Hawk cars — Bearcats to DV-32s — with a quarterly magazine and the Grand Stutz gathering at the centre of the calendar.
clubs.name: The Stutz Club

clubs.chapterModel: Local groups across the UK and worldwide membership
clubs.description: The TR sports cars' club since 1970 — tens of thousands of members over its life, deep technical archives for TR2 to TR8, and the annual international weekend.
clubs.name: TR Register

clubs.description: The UK home of the Big Healeys and Sprites — centres in every region, a sprint and hillclimb championship, and six decades of accumulated knowledge on keeping Donald Healey's cars competitive.
clubs.name: Austin Healey Club

clubs.chapterModel: Regional areas across the UK and international membership
clubs.description: The Jensen club since 1971 — Interceptor, FF, C-V8, 541 and Jensen-Healey all under one roof, with registrars for each model and an annual international meeting.
clubs.name: Jensen Owners' Club

clubs.description: The Blackpool cars' owners' club — regional meets, the Sprint magazine, and the collective knowledge for keeping glassfibre TVRs from Grantura to Sagaris on the road.
clubs.name: TVR Car Club

clubs.chapterModel: Umbrella for the regional Austin Seven clubs
clubs.description: The umbrella body for Britain's Austin Seven clubs since 1969 — the Association magazine, the production-figure archive, and the network that keeps the Seven's centenary-era scene organised.
clubs.name: Austin Seven Clubs' Association

clubs.description: The British club for Carl Borgward's cars — Hansa, Isabella, Arabella and P100 — with the spares knowledge and remanufacture contacts that an orphaned marque depends on.
clubs.name: Borgward Drivers Club

clubs.description: The Pantera and De Tomaso club in the US since 1979 — chapter events, the POCA newsletter and profiles, and the technical archive for keeping Ford-powered Modena cars on American roads.
clubs.name: Pantera Owners Club of America

note: Seed registry of real, established clubs and club networks. Waves 1–2: national-level entries for most marques, with chapter-level entries (regional chapters with their own calendars) beginning in wave 2. Wave 3 adds the marque clubs for the historic batch — Duesenberg (via the ACD Club), Packard, Saab, Studebaker, DeLorean, Pontiac and Oldsmobile. Wave 5 adds the historic batch 2 clubs — Hudson, Nash, Kaiser, Stutz, Triumph, Austin-Healey, Jensen and TVR; Cord is served by the Auburn Cord Duesenberg Club already listed. Location discovery filters by region and marque; chapter-level geo data (city, meeting cadence, member counts) expands in later waves. Club details were accurate as seeded — verify current membership terms on each club's own site before joining.
